description: HTTPS: a zero-length TLS write re-enters `llhttp_execute()`, and the server copies its own heap into the request body
overview: A re-entrancy flaw in Node.js HTTPS lets an unauthenticated client read memory belonging to other connections, including TLS private keys and other users' requests. `TLSWrap::DoWrite()` calls `ClearOut()` directly when asked to write zero bytes; if that write is issued from JavaScript running inside the HTTP parser's `on_body` callback, `ClearOut()` decrypts the next TLS record while the parser is still mid-body, re-entering `llhttp_execute()` and causing a use-after-free and an out-of-bounds heap read. The server then copies that freed or unrelated heap memory into the response for the request body. Triggering it requires a handler that calls `res.flushHeaders()` before the request body ends and later calls `res.end()` with a non-empty chunk, and reading the leaked memory requires any ordinary route that echoes or stores a request body. Cleartext `node:http` is not affected. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.
